title: Lesson 37 derived action and patientive NNC review

groups.title: Deverbal Source foundation
groups.proposal: Build the Lesson 37 nounstem from the verbcore of an exact owner-issued VNC Result. Preserve the complete typed verbstem Source and its internal boundaries; do not treat the whole predicate as the nounstem and do not authorize the route by the example verb.
groups.readingJob: Show the VNC Result, the verbcore selected from it, the resulting NNC Source, and why the operation is derivation rather than simple predicate reanalysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a licensed deverbal formation only when more than one formation is genuinely possible; the application identifies the verbcore and preserves its Source analysis automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a copied-predicate, example-stem, formula, surface, or manual-boundary control.

groups.title: Active-action NNCs in z
groups.proposal: Derive the restricted active-action nounstem in z from a compatible typed future verbcore, preserve the source subject as the NNC possessor, and derive its action, process, result, state, class, number, supportive-vowel, and final-shape behavior. Treat rare compatibility and lexical meanings as typed lexical facts, never as a list of permitted stems.
groups.readingJob: Show future-core ancestry without confusing nominal z with tense z, subject-to-possessor continuity, final i or replacive i, class and number, morphemic Source shape, and narrow lexical readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses z only where the typed Source and lexical analysis license that genuine alternative; the application derives participant transfer, supportive or replacive vowel behavior, class, and number.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not whitelist examples, infer rare compatibility from spelling alone, or expose automatic i, class, number, or participant transfer as choices.

groups.title: Active-action NNCs in liz
groups.proposal: Derive the productive active-action nounstem in liz from the typed verbcore, with l plus supportive i plus z, class-conditioned final-vowel behavior, retained projective or reflexive participants, and the licensed loss of supportive i after tla or ne. Keep typed Source history even where different analyses sound alike.
groups.readingJob: Show l-i-z structure, Source class, vowel deletion or retention, object and reflexive placement, supportive-i loss, Source history, and active-action meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses liz as the intended licensed formation and chooses only a genuinely free variant; the application derives all class, boundary, vowel, and participant consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual l, i, z, vowel-length, object-placement, example-stem, or copied-formula controls.

groups.title: liz replacive-stem families
groups.proposal: Apply the licensed ca to qui, hua to hui or retained hua, ci to xi, and optional ti to chi changes from typed morphemic Source shape and lexical analysis. Preserve frequentative destockal history and licensed variants without turning the examples into a route list.
groups.readingJob: Show the underlying Source, relevant boundary, replacive outcome, retained alternative, destockal history, and whether a variant is productive or lexical.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a licensed lexical or free variant; predictable boundary behavior is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not authorize an alternation by exact stem identity unless Canvas makes the fact genuinely lexical.

groups.title: Root plus ya behavior before liz
groups.proposal: Preserve root-plus-ya structure and apply deletion or retention before liz according to typed derivational and lexical analysis, including the denominal ti-ya and hui-ya patterns. Do not decide the route from the visible final letters alone.
groups.readingJob: Show root, ya, derivational layer, deletion or retention, denominal history, and any genuine variant.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a licensed retained or deleted variant where Canvas leaves both available; otherwise the application applies the typed analysis automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not flatten ya into the root or create an exact-example admission list.

groups.title: Way-of and lexicalized liz readings
groups.proposal: Keep the compositional active-action reading available while preserving narrow way-of and other lexicalized readings as typed lexical facts. Retain exact lexical matrix identity only where Canvas makes it genuinely fixed, such as ca-h.
groups.readingJob: Show the compositional action meaning, licensed lexical extension, and the Source fact that supports the reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses among genuinely available readings when context does not resolve them; the application does not infer lexical meaning from liz alone.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not generalize way-of meaning or fixed-matrix behavior to unrelated Sources.

groups.title: Compound active-action Sources
groups.proposal: Derive z and liz action nounstems from complete compound verbcores while preserving every internal Source constituent and boundary. Read connective t plus the matrix on-o correctly and keep lexical compound meanings typed.
groups.readingJob: Show embed, connective or derivational material, matrix, internal participants, boundaries, action suffix, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended licensed action formation or lexical reading; the application preserves and interprets compound structure automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create a separate t-o verbstem class, flatten a compound into a string, or whitelist witnessed compounds.

groups.title: Active-action and potential-patient contrast
groups.proposal: Keep active-action and potential-patient Sources distinct even when an intransitive third-person singular form is homophonous. Use typed valence, participant structure, object retention or absence, and person-number facts; expose a meaning choice only where the grammatical evidence leaves a real ambiguity.
groups.readingJob: Show agent/action versus potential-patient meaning, object retention or absence, third-singular ambiguity, disambiguating person-number facts, and narrow exceptions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended reading only for a genuine unresolved homophony; the application resolves all cases fixed by typed structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not decide from English translation or surface identity and do not erase reflexive-plus-tla exceptions.

groups.title: General-action NNCs from impersonal Sources
groups.proposal: Derive the general-action liz nounstem from an exact impersonal VNC Result, whether impersonalization comes from nonactive structure or impersonal tla. Preserve the source owner, shuntline facts, and lexical readings while treating spelling cautions as reading guidance.
groups.readingJob: Show the impersonal source pathway, retained participants, action meaning, lexical extension, and any spelling warning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a licensed impersonal Source analysis or an unresolved reading; the application derives the general-action structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not invent an impersonal source from the nounstem surface and do not make a misspelling a grammar option.

groups.title: Action NNC continuations
groups.proposal: Allow an exact owner-issued active-action NNC Result to serve as the embedded Source of licensed VNC and NNC compounds. Preserve its complete canonical Source and semantic relation through continuation, including boundary-driven assimilation and lexical compound readings.
groups.readingJob: Show the captured action NNC, embed-matrix relation, boundary changes, resulting family, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended licensed matrix and semantic relation; the application preserves the embedded Result and derives boundary behavior.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not continue from a copied string, guessed surface, or example identity.

groups.title: z and liz before tzin
groups.proposal: Apply the boundary-driven s-to-tz assimilation where a z or liz action Source meets the tzin matrix, while keeping ordinary spelling and the fuller underlying Source analysis available for reading.
groups.readingJob: Show the underlying z or liz, following tzin, phonological outcome, conventional spelling, and preserved morphemic analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives the assimilation; the user makes no new grammar choice.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose assimilation or doubled spelling as a user control.

groups.title: Active-action and passive-action contrast
groups.proposal: Keep active-action and passive-action NNCs distinct by their typed VNC ancestry. In possessive state, interpret the possessor as agent for active action and patient for passive action, even when translations or forms overlap.
groups.readingJob: Show active or passive Source, possessor role, action or result meaning, and any surface overlap.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended Source analysis only where it is genuinely ambiguous; the application derives the possessor role from typed voice.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer voice from translation or let the user manually relabel the possessor role.

groups.title: Action NNC supplementation
groups.proposal: Allow an exact owner-issued active-action NNC Result to serve as a supplementary object alongside a compatible VNC supplement. Reuse the shared supplementation owner and decide compatibility from typed clause roles and referent identity, not from the action nounstem.
groups.readingJob: Show principal and supplement Results, shared referent, participant role, supplementation link, and clause meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses principal and supplement only when more than one valid link remains; the application checks referent and participant compatibility and acyclicity.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add Lesson 37 supplementation machinery or authorize a link from surface similarity.

groups.title: Patientive taxonomy and Source truncation
groups.proposal: Represent patientives as typed derivations from passive, impersonal, perfective-active, imperfective-active, or root-stock Sources. Apply the licensed nonactive truncation patterns from complete morphemic Source structure, while requiring typed lexical analysis for idiosyncratic formations and meanings.
groups.readingJob: Show patientive meaning range, exact Source family, removed nonactive material, retained boundary and vowel behavior, noun class, and lexical exception status.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended Source family or lexical analysis when grammar cannot derive it; the application performs regular truncation automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer patientive family or lexical meaning from final letters alone and do not treat the outline examples as a whitelist.

groups.title: Passive-patientive foundation
groups.proposal: Derive a passive patientive only from an exact passive VNC Result, never from an intransitive Source. Preserve nonspecific projective or shuntline reflexive evidence, with the licensed no-object passive branch handled explicitly rather than guessed.
groups.readingJob: Show active ancestry, passive Result, object or shuntline evidence, patient referent, and the specific no-object branch when applicable.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies any genuinely required source or lexical analysis; the application validates passive ancestry and blocks incompatible intransitive input.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create a passive history from a patientive surface or allow an untyped intransitive source.

groups.title: lō passive-patientives
groups.proposal: Derive the lō-family passive patientive by deleting final ō while retaining l and applying the licensed preceding-vowel behavior. Preserve complete passive ancestry, object facts, noun class, and narrow lexical or figurative readings.
groups.readingJob: Show passive lō Source, deleted ō, retained l, preceding vowel behavior, active ancestry, participant structure, class, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading or licensed variant; regular truncation follows automatically from the typed boundary.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not whitelist examples or reconstruct passive ancestry from the shortened nounstem.

groups.title: ō passive-patientives
groups.proposal: Derive the ō-family passive patientive by deleting the complete passive suffix and preserving the typed active and passive Source chain, participant facts, referent type, noun class, and licensed lexicalized meanings.
groups.readingJob: Show active Source, passive ō layer, deleted suffix, resulting patientive Source, referent type, participants, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading; the application derives regular truncation and participant continuity.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not treat spouse, messenger, flour, neck, or other examples as route permission.

groups.title: hua passive-patientives
groups.proposal: Derive the hua-family passive patientive by deleting hua and shortening preceding ī where licensed, while preserving supportive-vowel analysis, reduplication, active ancestry, unexpected nonactive sources, and Nahuatl patientive construals that may differ from English intuition.
groups.readingJob: Show hua deletion, vowel shortening, supportive vowels, reduplication, active and passive ancestry, lexical meaning, irregular-source status, and patientive construal.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies a genuinely needed irregular lexical analysis or chooses an open reading; the application applies regular hua-boundary behavior automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not reject an owner-authorized irregular nonactive Source and do not replace Nahuatl grammar with English semantic intuition.

groups.title: Reflexive passive-patientives
groups.proposal: Preserve the shuntline reflexive ne from an exact reflexive passive VNC Result inside the derived patientive nounstem, together with its active reflexive ancestry and licensed lexical meanings.
groups.readingJob: Show active reflexive Source, passive shuntline ne, patientive derivation, referent, and compositional or lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a genuinely open lexical reading; reflexive inheritance is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not manually insert ne or reconstruct reflexivity from the final surface.

groups.title: Double-object passive-patientives
groups.proposal: Derive passive patientives from exact double-object VNC Results while retaining only the licensed surviving object pronoun. Preserve which participant becomes the patientive referent, which object remains internal, and the licensed optional deletion of tē.
groups.readingJob: Show active double-object roles, passive promotion, surviving internal object, patientive referent, optional tē deletion, and lexical meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses only a licensed tē variant or genuinely open participant interpretation; the application derives all participant-role consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose arbitrary object deletion or infer participant roles from prefix order alone.
